title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations Studies On The Effects Of Mutations On The Binding Affinities Between SARS-CoV-2 Spike RBD And Human ACE2
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子动力学模拟研究SARS-CoV-2刺突蛋白RBD与ACE2突变体的结合亲和力变化，虽属蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白-DNA体系，但MD与界面结合能分析方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作研究，相关性有限。
abstract: CONSPECTUS The SARS-CoV-2 viruses had made a great impact on humankind and the world economy. Phylogenetic analysis revealed the newly identified B.1.617.1 and B.1.617.2 lineages possessed with few key mutations predominantly circulating. The signature mutations possessed by these lineages are situated in the RBD motif of S protein. Reports revealed variants L452R, T478K, and E484Q harbours in enhancement with hACE2 binding while P681R situated in furin cleavage site resulting in better transmissibility. To gain a deeper understanding of the impact of these variants (L452R, T478K and E484Q) binding with hACE2, structural dynamics at the interface between S-RBD protein and hACE2 were studied. We performed our dynamics studies with both single mutant complex (L452R, T478K and E484Q) and in the combination of triple mutants (L452R + T478K + E484Q) at 100ns in contrast with the wild type. Interfacial docking interactions and Molecular Mechanics approach exhibited that the spike mutants −L452R, T478K and E484Q harbour with higher binding affinity on hACE2 in contrast with its native spike protein. The presence of interfacial residue, intermolecular contacts such as hydrogen bonding, salt bridge and non-hydrogen bonded interactions might be the reason for its higher binding affinity. Hence the findings from our study unravelled plausible mechanism for the increase in affinities of mutants to hACE2 thus leading to higher transmissibility and infection of emerging variants. Further, the conformational alterations in the course of dynamics at the RBD motif led to enhancement of hACE2 binding and immune escape. These results suggest that the structural changes introduced by these variants enhance the binding affinities of the S protein with the hACE2 that could form the basis to further aid in designing therapeutics that could inhibit at the interface of S protein and hACE2 receptor.
abstract_zh: 概要 SARS-CoV-2病毒对人类和世界经济产生了巨大影响。系统发育分析显示，新发现的B.1.617.1和B.1.617.2谱系携带几个关键突变，并主要流行。这些谱系所携带的特征性突变位于S蛋白的RBD基序中。报道显示，L452R、T478K和E484Q变异增强了与hACE2的结合，而位于弗林蛋白酶切割位点的P681R则导致更高的传播性。为了更深入理解这些变异（L452R、T478K和E484Q）与hACE2结合的影响，我们研究了S-RBD蛋白与hACE2界面处的结构动力学。我们进行了100ns的动力学研究，包括单突变复合物（L452R、T478K和E484Q）以及三突变组合（L452R + T478K + E484Q），并与野生型进行对比。界面对接相互作用和分子力学方法表明，刺突突变体−L452R、T478K和E484Q与hACE2的结合亲和力高于其天然刺突蛋白。界面残基的存在、分子间接触（如氢键、盐桥和非氢键相互作用）可能是其更高结合亲和力的原因。因此，我们的研究结果揭示了突变体对hACE2亲和力增加的潜在机制，从而导致新变异株更高的传播性和感染性。此外，在动力学过程中RBD基序的构象变化增强了hACE2结合和免疫逃逸。这些结果表明，这些变异引入的结构变化增强了S蛋白与hACE2的结合亲和力，这可能为进一步设计在S蛋白和hACE2受体界面处抑制的治疗药物提供基础。
